nodes.title: SG-5.5 · Scheduler behavior with a fake clock unit tests
nodes.body:
Context: backend/internal/round/scheduler.go already implements Scheduler.Tick with an injected Clock, Controller and Lister. backend/internal/round/scheduler_test.go already holds tests using fakeClock, fakeController and fakeLister. Desired behavior: the four named scheduler behaviors are covered by passing unit tests that use only fakes. Expected result: go test for those tests passes. Why: the round lifecycle must open and close rounds on time without a real clock.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round whose StartsAt is before the fake clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Open is called once for that round and Close is not called
- Given an OPEN round whose EndsAt is before the fake clock time, when Tick runs, then Controller.Close is called once for that round
- Given future-start SCHEDULED, future-end OPEN and COMPLETED rounds, when Tick runs before the boundary, then no Controller call is made, and when the clock reaches the boundary, then only the due Open and Close calls are made
- Given Controller.Open returns an error and another round is due for Close, when Tick runs, then Tick returns an error wrapping the Open error and Close is still called for the other round


## Scope
- In scope: Scheduler.Tick behavior with a fake clock
- In scope: Unit tests in backend/internal/round/scheduler_test.go
- Out of scope: Scheduler.Run ticker loop
- Out of scope: Real Controller, store or Git behavior
- Out of scope: Admin routes and server wiring
- Preserve: Scheduler, Clock, Controller and Lister public signatures
- Preserve: Tick error joining via errors.Join


## Technical constraints
- Go standard testing package only
- No real clock, sleep, filesystem or network in the tests


## Definition of done
- All four Tick behaviors are asserted by passing unit tests


## Non-functional requirements
- Tests finish in milliseconds


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Tick opens due SCHEDULED rounds, closes expired OPEN rounds and waits for future and COMPLETED rounds
nodes.body:
Context: Scheduler.Tick in backend/internal/round/scheduler.go compares clock.Now() with StartsAt for SCHEDULED rounds and EndsAt for OPEN rounds. Desired behavior: due rounds are opened or closed, while future-start, future-end and COMPLETED rounds are ignored until the boundary. Expected result: Controller receives exactly the due Open and Close calls. Why: rounds must change state at the right time.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a SCHEDULED round with StartsAt 11:00 and clock 12:00, when Tick runs, then Open is called with the world ID and round ID
- Given an OPEN round with EndsAt 11:59 and clock 12:00, when Tick runs, then Close is called with the world ID and round ID
- Given future SCHEDULED, future OPEN and COMPLETED rounds at clock 12:00, when Tick runs, then no calls are made, and at clock 13:00 only Open and Close for the two non-COMPLETED rounds are made


## Scope
- In scope: Tick switch cases on Status and clock boundary
- Out of scope: Error aggregation behavior
- Preserve: !now.Before(boundary) comparison so the exact boundary instant counts as due


## Technical constraints
- Time comes only from Scheduler.Clock


## Definition of done
- Tick dispatch against the clock is confirmed in scheduler.go and covered by tests


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Tick returns an Open failure and still closes another due round
nodes.body:
Context: Tick appends errors to a slice and returns errors.Join(errs...) after the loop. Desired behavior: an Open error is wrapped and returned while Close for another due round still runs. Expected result: errors.Is(err, openErr) is true and both calls are recorded. Why: one failing round must not block another round from closing.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given Open returns an error for a due SCHEDULED round, when Tick runs, then the returned error satisfies errors.Is with that error
- Given an expired OPEN round listed after the failing round, when Tick runs, then Close is still called for it and calls are open then close in order


## Scope
- In scope: Error collection and joining in Tick
- Out of scope: Retry of failed opens
- Preserve: Error wrapping with %w in the open and close messages


## Technical constraints
- Use errors.Join and fmt.Errorf with %w


## Definition of done
- Error behavior is confirmed in scheduler.go and covered by a test


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Confirm Tick collects errors and continues after a Controller failure
nodes.body:
Tick appends wrapped errors and returns errors.Join. Read it and make it match; change nothing if it already does. Result: an Open failure is returned and later rounds are still processed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tick never returns early from the rounds loop on an Open or Close error
- The returned error wraps the Controller error so errors.Is matches it

- Preserve: Error messages prefixed with round: open and round: close
